claim: Nrn1 was initially discovered as a neurotrophic factor linked to the neuronal cell membrane through a glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor.
source: Nrn1, also known as candidate plasticity gene 15 (CPG15), was initially discovered as a neurotrophic factor linked to the neuronal cell membrane through a glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor (Nedivi et al., 1998; Zhou and Zhou, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Nedivi et al., 1998; Zhou and Zhou, 2014).

claim: Nrn1 is highly conserved across species, with 96% overall homology between the murine and human protein.
source: It is highly conserved across species, with 96% overall homology between the murine and human protein.
evidence: The claim is stated as established knowledge about Nrn1 protein conservation.

claim: Nrn1 plays multiple roles in neural development, synaptic plasticity, synaptic maturation, neuronal migration, and survival.
source: Nrn1 plays multiple roles in neural development, synaptic plasticity, synaptic maturation, neuronal migration, and survival (Cantallops et al., 2000; Javaherian and Cline, 2005; Nedivi et al., 1998; Putz et al., 2005; Zito et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published research.

claim: Nrn1 expression has been found in FOXP3+ Treg and follicular regulatory T cells (Tfr).
source: In the immune system, Nrn1 expression has been found in FOXP3+ Treg and follicular regulatory T cells (Tfr; Gonzalez-Figueroa et al., 2021; Vahl et al., 2014)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Nrn1 expression has been found in T cells from transplant tolerant recipients.
source: T cells from transplant tolerant recipients (Lim et al., 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published work.

claim: Nrn1 expression has been found in anergized CD8 cells or CD8 cells from tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in mouse tumor models.
source: anergized CD8 cells or CD8 cells from tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in mouse tumor models (Schietinger et al., 2012; Schietinger et al., 2016; Singer et al., 2016)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Nrn1 expression has been found in human Treg infiltrating breast cancer tumor tissue.
source: in human Treg infiltrating breast cancer tumor tissue (Plitas et al., 2016)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published work.

claim: Soluble Nrn1 can be released from Tfr cells and act directly on B cells to suppress autoantibody development against tissue-specific antigens.
source: Soluble Nrn1 can be released from Tfr cells and act directly on B cells to suppress autoantibody development against tissue-specific antigens (Gonzalez-Figueroa et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Nrn1 expression was significantly higher among cells recovered from C3-HA hosts vs. cells from VacHA infected mice at all time points tested by qRT-PCR.
source: Nrn1 expression was significantly higher among cells recovered from C3-HA hosts vs. cells from VacHA infected mice at all time points tested by qRT-PCR (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A using qRT-PCR measurements.

claim: Nrn1 expression was significantly higher in Ta than in naïve CD4 (Tn) and antigen-experienced cells (Te) under steady-state conditions measured by both qRT-PCR and western blot.
source: Nrn1 expression was significantly higher in Ta than in naïve CD4 (Tn, CD4+CD62L+CD44-FR4-CD73-) and antigen-experienced cells (Te, CD4+CD44+FR4-CD73-) under steady-state conditions measured by both qRT-PCR and western blot (Figure 1BFigure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B using qRT-PCR and western blot.

claim: Nrn1 expression can be detected in nTreg and induced Treg (iTreg) cells generated in vitro.
source: Nrn1 expression can be detected in nTreg and induced Treg (iTreg) cells generated in vitro (Figure 1C, Figure 1—source data 3 and 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Nrn1 mRNA level was significantly increased among tumor-associated Treg cells and non-Treg CD4 cells compared to cells from peripheral blood.
source: Nrn1 mRNA level was significantly increased among tumor-associated Treg cells and non-Treg CD4 cells compared to cells from peripheral blood (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Treg and non-Treg T cells from human breast cancer infiltrates reveal significantly higher Nrn1 expression compared to the peripheral blood Treg and non-Treg cells.
source: Consistent with our findings in the mouse tumor setting, the Treg and non-Treg T cells from human breast cancer infiltrates reveal significantly higher Nrn1 expression compared to the peripheral blood Treg and non-Treg cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B; Plitas et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by data from Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and citation to published work.

claim: Nrn1 expression was significantly induced after CD4+ T cell activation.
source: Nrn1 expression was significantly induced after CD4+ T cell activation (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: NRN1 can be detected on activated CD4+ and CD8+ cells using an NRN1-specific monoclonal antibody.
source: Using an NRN1-specific, monoclonal antibody, NRN1 can be detected on activated CD4+ and CD8+ cells (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Nrn1-/- mice had consistently reduced body weight compared to heterozygous Nrn1+/-, WT (Nrn1+/+) mice.
source: In the first evaluation of the Nrn1-/- colony, Nrn1-/- mice had consistently reduced body weight compared to heterozygous Nrn1+/-, WT (Nrn1+/+) mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The lymphoid tissues of Nrn1-/- mice were comparable to their Nrn1+/-, WT counterparts except for a slight reduction in cell number that was observed in the spleens of Nrn1-/- mice.
source: The lymphoid tissues of Nrn1-/- mice were comparable to their Nrn1+/-, WT counterparts except for a slight reduction in cell number that was observed in the spleens of Nrn1-/- mice, likely due to their smaller size (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Analysis of thymocytes revealed no defect in T cell development in Nrn1-/- mice.
source: Analysis of thymocytes revealed no defect in T cell development (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: A flow cytometric survey of the major immune cell populations in the peripheral lymphoid tissue revealed similar proportions of CD4, CD8 T cells, B cells, monocytes and dendritic cells (DCs) in Nrn1-/-, Nrn1+/-, WT mice.
source: a flow cytometric survey of the major immune cell populations in the peripheral lymphoid tissue of these mice revealed similar proportions of CD4, CD8 T cells, B cells, monocytes and dendritic cells (DCs; Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: No differences were found between the proportions of anergic and Treg cells in Nrn1-/-, Nrn1+/-, WT mice.
source: Similarly, no differences were found between the proportions of anergic and Treg cells in Nrn1-/-, Nrn1+/-, WT mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E, F)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E, F.

claim: Histopathology assessment of lung, heart, liver, kidney, intestine, and spleen harvested from 13 months old Nrn1-/- and Nrn1+/- did not reveal any evidence of autoimmunity.
source: Additionally, histopathology assessment of lung, heart, liver, kidney, intestine, and spleen harvested from 13 months old Nrn1-/- and Nrn1+/- did not reveal any evidence of autoimmunity (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is stated based on histopathology assessment data.

claim: The proportion and number of OTII cells increased in the Nrn1-/-_OTII compared to the ctrl_OTII hosts on day 13 after cell transfer.
source: On day 13 after cell transfer, the proportion and number of OTII cells increased in the Nrn1-/-_OTII compared to the ctrl_OTII hosts (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Nrn1-/-_OTII cells produced increased IL2 than ctrl_OTII upon restimulation.
source: Moreover, Nrn1-/-_OTII cells produced increased IL2 than ctrl_OTII upon restimulation (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The proportion of FOXP3+ pTreg among Nrn1-/-_OTII was significantly reduced.
source: Consistent with reduced anergy induction, the proportion of FOXP3+ pTreg among Nrn1-/-_OTII was significantly reduced (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The gene set on T cell anergy was enriched in ctrl relative to Nrn1-/-_OTII cells.
source: Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed that the gene set on T cell anergy was enriched in ctrl relative to Nrn1-/-_OTII cells (Figure 1I; Safford et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 1I and citation to published gene set.

claim: The Treg signature gene set was prominently reduced in Nrn1-/-_OTII cells relative to the ctrl.
source: Also, consistent with the decreased transdifferentiation to FOXP3+ cells, the Treg signature gene set was prominently reduced in Nrn1-/-_OTII cells relative to the ctrl (Figure 1J).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 1J.

claim: Nrn1-/- CD4+ cells showed reduced T cell activation, as evidenced by reduced CellTrace violet dye (CTV) dilution, activation marker expression, and Ca++ entry after TCR stimulation.
source: Nrn1-/- CD4+ cells showed reduced T cell activation, as evidenced by reduced CellTrace violet dye (CTV) dilution, activation marker expression, and Ca++ entry after TCR stimulation (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, B, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, B, C.

claim: Similar proportions of FOXP3+ cells were observed in Nrn1-/- and ctrl cells under the iTreg culture condition.
source: Similar proportions of FOXP3+ cells were observed in Nrn1-/- and ctrl cells under the iTreg culture condition (Figure 2A)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Reduced live cells over time were found in Nrn1-/- iTreg compared to the ctrl after restimulation with anti-CD3.
source: To examine the capacity of iTreg expansion, Nrn1-/- and ctrl iTreg cells were restimulated with anti-CD3, and we found reduced live cells over time in Nrn1-/- iTreg compared to the ctrl (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The reduced live cell number in Nrn1-/- iTreg was accompanied by reduced Ki67 expression.
source: The reduced live cell number in Nrn1-/- was accompanied by reduced Ki67 expression (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Nrn1-/- iTregs retained a higher proportion of FOXP3+ cells 3 days after restimulation.
source: Although Nrn1-/- iTregs retained a higher proportion of FOXP3+ cells 3 days after restimulation, however, when taking into account the total number of live cells, the actual number of live FOXP3+ cells was reduced in Nrn1-/- (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The actual number of live FOXP3+ cells was reduced in Nrn1-/- iTreg 3 days after restimulation.
source: Although Nrn1-/- iTregs retained a higher proportion of FOXP3+ cells 3 days after restimulation, however, when taking into account the total number of live cells, the actual number of live FOXP3+ cells was reduced in Nrn1-/- (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Nrn1-/- nTreg cells retained a higher FOXP3+ cell proportion and reduced Ki67 expression compared to the ctrl at day 7 post transfer.
source: Although the CD45.1-CD45.2+ Nrn1-/- and ctrl cell proportions were not significantly different among hosts splenocytes at day 7 post transfer (Figure 2F), Nrn1-/- cells retained a higher FOXP3+ cell proportion and reduced Ki67 expression comparing to the ctrl (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G and H.

claim: Nrn1-/- Tregs showed reduced suppression toward CD45.1+ responder cells, evidenced by increased CD45.1+ proportion and cell number in host splenocytes.
source: Nrn1-/- Tregs also showed reduced suppression toward CD45.1+ responder cells, evidenced by increased CD45.1+ proportion and cell number in host splenocytes (Figure 2I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Tumors grew much slower in Nrn1-/- Treg recipients than those reconstituted with ctrl Tregs.
source: Tumors grew much slower in Nrn1-/- Treg recipients than those reconstituted with ctrl Tregs (Figure 2J).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2J.

claim: The number of CD45.1+ cells in tumor-draining lymph nodes and spleens increased significantly in Nrn1-/- Treg hosts compared to the ctrl group.
source: Moreover, the number of CD45.1+ cells in tumor-draining lymph nodes and spleens increased significantly in Nrn1-/- Treg hosts compared to the ctrl group (Figure 2K).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2K.

claim: The CD45.1+ responder cell proportion among tumor lymphocyte infiltrates (TILs) was increased in Nrn1-/- Treg hosts.
source: Consistently, the CD45.1+ responder cell proportion among tumor lymphocyte infiltrates (TILs) was also increased (Figure 2L)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2L.

claim: An increased proportion of IFNγ + cells among CD8 TILs was observed from Nrn1-/- Treg hosts.
source: accompanied by an increased proportion of IFNγ + cells among CD8 TILs from Nrn1-/- Treg hosts (Figure 2M).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2M.

claim: Three clusters were enriched in resting Nrn1-/- iTreg identified by GSEA on gene ontology database and clustering of enriched gene sets by Cytoscape.
source: GSEA on gene ontology database and clustering of enriched gene sets by Cytoscape identified three clusters enriched in resting Nrn1-/- iTreg (Figure 3A, Figure 3—source data 1; Shannon et al., 2003; Subramanian et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 3A and citations to analysis methods.

claim: The 'neurotransmitter involved in membrane potential (MP)' and 'sodium transport' clusters involved gene sets on the ion transport and cell MP regulation.
source: The 'neurotransmitter involved in membrane potential (MP)' and 'sodium transport' clusters involved gene sets on the ion transport and cell MP regulation (Figure 3A, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The 'Neurotransmitter receptor activity involved in regulation of postsynaptic membrane potential' gene set was significantly enriched under resting and activation conditions in Nrn1-/- cells.
source: The 'Neurotransmitter receptor activity involved in regulation of postsynaptic membrane potential' gene set was significantly enriched under resting and activation conditions In Nrn1-/- cells (Figure 3C and D; Figure 3—source data 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The AMPAR subunits Gria2 and Gria3 showed increased expression in Nrn1-/- cells.
source: The α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor (AMPAR) subunits Gria2 and Gria3 are the major components of this gene set and showed increased expression in Nrn1-/- cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Nrn1 has been reported as an accessory protein for AMPAR.
source: Nrn1 has been reported as an accessory protein for AMPAR (Pandya et al., 2018; Schwenk et al., 2012; Subramanian et al., 2019)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Nrn1-/- iTreg exhibits significant hyperpolarization under both resting and activation conditions compared to ctrl iTreg cells.
source: Compared to ctrl iTreg cells, Nrn1-/- exhibits significant hyperpolarization under both resting and activation conditions (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by membrane potential measurement data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The 'MF_metal ion transmembrane transporter activity' gene set was significantly enriched and showed a different expression pattern in Nrn1-/- iTregs.
source: Consistent with the MP change, the 'MF_metal ion transmembrane transporter activity' gene set, which contains 436 ion channel related genes, was significantly enriched and showed a different expression pattern in Nrn1-/- iTregs (Figure 3F; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 3F and supplementary figures.

claim: Differential AA transporter gene expression was found between Nrn1-/- and ctrl iTregs.
source: we surveyed AA transport-related gene expression using the 'Amino acid transmembrane transporter activity' gene set and found differential AA transporter gene expression between Nrn1-/- and ctrl iTregs (Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The AA-induced cellular MP change was reduced in Nrn1-/- iTreg compared to the ctrl.
source: The AA-induced cellular MP change was reduced in Nrn1-/- compared to the ctrl, reflective of differential AA transporter expression patterns (Figure 3H).
evidence: The claim is supported by membrane potential measurement data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Reduced phosphorylation of mTOR and S6 was found in activated Nrn1-/- iTreg cells.
source: We examined mTORC1 activation at the protein level by evaluating mTOR and S6 phosphorylation via flow cytometry. We found reduced phosphorylation of mTOR and S6 in activated Nrn1-/- iTreg cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The degree of mTOR and S6 phosphorylation change after nutrient sensing was significantly less in Nrn1-/- iTreg than in the ctrl.
source: While adding the medium with nutrients clearly increased the mTOR and S6 phosphorylation, the degree of change was significantly less in Nrn1-/- than in the ctrl (Figure 3I).
evidence: The claim is supported by nutrient sensing assay data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Nrn1-/- iTreg cells showed reduced expression of glycolysis, fatty acid metabolism, and oxidative phosphorylation related gene sets under both resting and activating conditions.
source: Moreover, Nrn1-/- cells also showed reduced expression of glycolysis, fatty acid metabolism, and oxidative phosphorylation related gene sets under both resting and activating conditions (Figure 3J, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 3J and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Reduced glycolysis was confirmed among Nrn1-/- iTreg cells by seahorse assay.
source: we performed the seahorse assay and confirmed reduced glycolysis among Nrn1-/- cells (Figure 3K).
evidence: The claim is supported by seahorse assay data shown in Figure 3K.

claim: A similar oxygen consumption rate (OCR) was observed between Nrn1-/- and ctrl iTreg cells.
source: Examination of mitochondrial bioenergetic function revealed a similar oxygen consumption rate (OCR) between Nrn1-/- and ctrl cells (Figure 3K).
evidence: The claim is supported by seahorse assay data shown in Figure 3K.

claim: Nrn1-/- naïve CD4 T cells showed similar resting MP and AA-induced MP changes compared to the ctrl cells.
source: The Nrn1-/- naïve CD4 T cells showed similar resting MP and AA-induced MP changes compared to the ctrl cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by membrane potential measurement data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: Comparable glycolysis and mitochondrial bioenergetic function were observed between Nrn1-/- naïve CD4 T cells and the ctrl.
source: We also observed comparable glycolysis and mitochondrial bioenergetic function between Nrn1-/- naïve CD4 T cells and the ctrl (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by seahorse assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: WT iTreg cells differentiated in the presence of Nrn1 antibody exhibit reduced resting MP, similar to Nrn1-/- cells.
source: WT iTreg cells differentiated in the presence of Nrn1 antibody exhibit reduced resting MP, similar to Nrn1-/- cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by membrane potential measurement data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: WT iTreg cells differentiated under NRN1 antibody blockade showed a similar phenotype as Nrn1-/- cells upon restimulation, with reduced live cell number, reduced Ki67 expression, and increased FOXP3+ cell proportion among live cells.
source: Moreover, upon restimulation, WT iTreg cells differentiated under NRN1 antibody blockade showed a similar phenotype as Nrn1-/- cells, with reduced live cell number, reduced Ki67 expression, and increased FOXP3+ cell proportion among live cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E, F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E, F.

claim: Nrn1 deficient CD4 Te cells showed increased Ki67 expression, associated with increased cytokine TNFa, Il2, and IFNγ expression upon restimulation.
source: Nrn1 deficient CD4 Te cells showed increased Ki67 expression, associated with increased cytokine TNFa, Il2, and IFNγ expression upon restimulation (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Accelerated weight loss was observed in Nrn1-/-_FDG mice upon administration of DT.
source: Upon administration of DT, we observed accelerated weight loss in Nrn1-/-_FDG mice, reflecting enhanced autoimmune inflammation (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: A significant increase in Ki67 expression and inflammatory cytokine TNFa, IL2, and IFNγ expression among Nrn1-/- CD4 cells was observed on day 6 post DT treatment.
source: Examination of T cell response revealed a significant increase in Ki67 expression and inflammatory cytokine TNFa, IL2, and IFNγ expression among Nrn1-/- CD4 cells on day 6 post DT treatment (Figure 4D)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The proportion of FOXP3+ cells was very low on day 6 post DT treatment and comparable between Nrn1-/- and the ctrl.
source: The proportion of FOXP3+ cells was very low on day 6 post DT treatment and comparable between Nrn1-/- and the ctrl (Figure 4E)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: A cluster of gene sets on 'membrane repolarization' was identified in Nrn1-/- Te cells by GSEA and Cytoscape analysis.
source: GSEA and Cytoscape analysis identified a cluster of gene sets on 'membrane repolarization', suggesting that Nrn1 may also be involved in the regulation of MP under Te context (Figure 4F, Figure 4—source data 1; Shannon et al., 2003; Subramanian et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 4F and citations to analysis methods.

claim: The 'membrane_repolarization' gene set was enriched in Nrn1-/- Te cells.
source: While the 'membrane_repolarization' gene set was enriched in Nrn1-/- (Figure 4G)
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The AMPAR subunit Gria3 expression was elevated in Nrn1-/- Te cells.
source: the 'Neurotransmitter receptor activity involved in regulation of postsynaptic membrane potential' gene set was no longer enriched, but the AMPAR subunit Gria3 expression was still elevated in Nrn1-/- Te cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: MP in Te cells was comparable between Nrn1-/- and ctrl.
source: Although MP in Te cells was comparable between Nrn1-/- and ctrl (Figure 4H)
evidence: The claim is supported by membrane potential measurement data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: The 'MF_metal ion transmembrane transporter activity' gene set was significantly enriched in Nrn1-/- Te cells with different gene expression patterns.
source: the 'MF_metal ion transmembrane transporter activity' gene set was significantly enriched in Nrn1-/- with different gene expression patterns (Figure 4I, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 4I and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The 'Amino acid transmembrane transporter activity' gene set was significantly enriched in Nrn1-/- Te cells than the ctrl.
source: Examination of nutrient transporters revealed that the 'Amino acid transmembrane transporter activity' gene set was significantly enriched in Nrn1-/- cells than the ctrl (Figure 4J).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 4J.

claim: AA entry caused enhanced MP change among Nrn1-/- Te than the ctrl.
source: AA entry caused enhanced MP change among Nrn1-/- Te than the ctrl, in contrast with the finding under iTreg cell context (Figure 4K).
evidence: The claim is supported by membrane potential measurement data shown in Figure 4K.

claim: Enhanced mTOR and S6 phosphorylation was found in Nrn1-/- Te cells.
source: Along with the enrichment of ion channel and nutrient transporter genes (Figure 4I and J), we found enhanced mTOR and S6 phosphorylation in Nrn1-/- Te cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Nrn1-/- Te showed increased mTOR and S6 phosphorylation after sensing ions and nutrients in RPMI medium.
source: Nrn1-/- Te showed increased mTOR and S6 phosphorylation after sensing ions and nutrients in RPMI medium (Figure 4L)
evidence: The claim is supported by nutrient sensing assay data shown in Figure 4L.

claim: Nrn1-/- Te cells showed enrichment of gene sets on glycolysis and proliferation.
source: Along with increased mTORC1 signaling, Nrn1-/- Te cells also showed enrichment of gene sets on glycolysis and proliferation (Figure 4M).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 4M.

claim: Increased glycolysis was confirmed in Nrn1-/- Te cells by seahorse assay, while the OCR remained comparable between Nrn1-/- and ctrl.
source: Evaluation of metabolic changes by seahorse confirmed increased glycolysis in Nrn1-/- cells, while the OCR remained comparable between Nrn1-/- and ctrl (Figure 4N).
evidence: The claim is supported by seahorse assay data shown in Figure 4N.

claim: The incidence and time to EAE onset in Nrn1-/- mice were comparable to the ctrl mice.
source: Upon EAE induction, the incidence and time to EAE onset in Nrn1-/- mice were comparable to the ctrl mice, but the severity, disease persistence, and body weight loss were increased in Nrn1-/- mice (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by EAE disease monitoring data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The severity, disease persistence, and body weight loss were increased in Nrn1-/- mice upon EAE induction.
source: Upon EAE induction, the incidence and time to EAE onset in Nrn1-/- mice were comparable to the ctrl mice, but the severity, disease persistence, and body weight loss were increased in Nrn1-/- mice (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by EAE disease monitoring data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Exacerbated EAE was associated with significantly increased CD45+ cell infiltrates in the Nrn1-/- spinal cord.
source: Exacerbated EAE was associated with significantly increased CD45+ cell infiltrates, increased CD4+ cell number, increased proportion of MOG-specific CD4 cells, and reduced proportion of FOXP3+ CD4 cells in the Nrn1-/- spinal cord (Figure 5B–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Exacerbated EAE was associated with increased CD4+ cell number in the Nrn1-/- spinal cord.
source: Exacerbated EAE was associated with significantly increased CD45+ cell infiltrates, increased CD4+ cell number, increased proportion of MOG-specific CD4 cells, and reduced proportion of FOXP3+ CD4 cells in the Nrn1-/- spinal cord (Figure 5B–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Exacerbated EAE was associated with increased proportion of MOG-specific CD4 cells in the Nrn1-/- spinal cord.
source: Exacerbated EAE was associated with significantly increased CD45+ cell infiltrates, increased CD4+ cell number, increased proportion of MOG-specific CD4 cells, and reduced proportion of FOXP3+ CD4 cells in the Nrn1-/- spinal cord (Figure 5B–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by tetramer staining data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Exacerbated EAE was associated with reduced proportion of FOXP3+ CD4 cells in the Nrn1-/- spinal cord.
source: Exacerbated EAE was associated with significantly increased CD45+ cell infiltrates, increased CD4+ cell number, increased proportion of MOG-specific CD4 cells, and reduced proportion of FOXP3+ CD4 cells in the Nrn1-/- spinal cord (Figure 5B–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Increased proportions of IFNγ+ and IL17+ CD4 cells were observed in Nrn1-/- mice remaining in the draining lymph node compared to the ctrl mice.
source: Moreover, we also observed increased proportions of IFNγ+ and IL17+ CD4 cells in Nrn1-/- mice remaining in the draining lymph node compared to the ctrl mice (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Peripheral T cell tolerance is important in restricting autoimmunity and minimizing collateral damage during active immune reactions.
source: Peripheral T cell tolerance is important in restricting autoimmunity and minimizing collateral damage during active immune reactions and is achieved via diverse mechanisms, including T cell anergy, regulatory T (Treg) cell mediated suppression, and effector T (Te) cell exhaustion or deletion (ElTanbouly and Noelle, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published work.

claim: Peripheral T cell tolerance is achieved via diverse mechanisms, including T cell anergy, regulatory T (Treg) cell mediated suppression, and effector T (Te) cell exhaustion or deletion.
source: Peripheral T cell tolerance is important in restricting autoimmunity and minimizing collateral damage during active immune reactions and is achieved via diverse mechanisms, including T cell anergy, regulatory T (Treg) cell mediated suppression, and effector T (Te) cell exhaustion or deletion (ElTanbouly and Noelle, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published work.

claim: T cell anergy is associated with reduced glycolysis.
source: For example, T cell anergy is associated with reduced glycolysis, whereas activated T effector cells exhibit increased glycolysis (Buck et al., 2017; Geltink et al., 2018; Peng and Li, 2023; Zheng et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Activated T effector cells exhibit increased glycolysis.
source: For example, T cell anergy is associated with reduced glycolysis, whereas activated T effector cells exhibit increased glycolysis (Buck et al., 2017; Geltink et al., 2018; Peng and Li, 2023; Zheng et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Cellular metabolic states depend on electrolyte and nutrient uptake from the microenvironment.
source: Cellular metabolic states depend on electrolyte and nutrient uptake from the microenvironment (Chapman and Chi, 2022; Olenchock et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Ion channels and nutrient transporters can integrate environmental nutrient changes and affect the cellular metabolic choices and impact the T cell functional outcome.
source: Ion channels and nutrient transporters, which can integrate environmental nutrient changes, affect the cellular metabolic choices and impact the T cell functional outcome (Babst, 2020; Bohmwald et al., 2021; Ramirez et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work.

claim: Anergic CD4 Tconv cells can transdifferentiate into FOXP3+ pTreg cells in vivo.
